fatal_errors: The proposed experimental strain-rate regime (10^-4 to 10^-1 s^-1) is wholly different from the molecular-dynamics regime of 10^8 to 10^10 s^-1.
Cross-slip is asserted as the governing mechanism, whereas the target behavior is mediated by vacancy-associated nucleation of Shockley partials and intrinsic/extrinsic stacking faults.
The baseline is changed to CoCrFeMnNi at ambient, quasistatic conditions instead of FeNiCrMn at 300 K and 10^9 s^-1.
The central claim of a strain-rate-dependent deformation transition misses the observed negligible strain-rate sensitivity of yield strength.
No evidence supports the premise that removing Co increases lattice distortion or produces greater cross-slip activity.
explanation: The response addresses temperature- and rate-dependent deformation of Co-free FeNiCrMn and gives a falsifiable comparison, but it does not reconstruct the relevant single-crystal molecular-dynamics study. Its temperatures, strain rates, baseline, and experimental modality differ substantially from the target. It also replaces the observed mechanism—defect-site nucleation of Shockley partials followed by stacking-fault formation—with an unsupported cross-slip transition. Only the general expectation of thermal softening overlaps with the result; it omits crystallographic anisotropy, strain-rate-insensitive yield, rate-enhanced dislocation density and flow stress, and the absence of BCC transformation or twinning. The proposed TEM comparison is testable but would not cleanly distinguish the target mechanism, and post-deformation images alone may not uniquely establish cross-slip.
